findings.title: Hang recovery does not kill spawned flusher processes
findings.body: Workers are always created with the explicit `spawn` context, which produces `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances. `SpawnProcess` is not an instance of the public default-context `multiprocessing.Process` class, so this guard is false for production workers. When a worker is deemed hung, the code starts a replacement for the same shard group without killing the old worker; the old process is then no longer tracked and can continue flushing/producing concurrently. Repeated health failures leak workers and can duplicate segment output. Test against the spawn-context process/base-process type (or simply use a `kill` capability check) and wait for the old worker before replacing it.

findings.title: Timed joins abandon remaining flusher workers
findings.body: Once `next_step.join(timeout)` or waiting for an earlier worker exhausts the deadline, this `break` exits the loop without attempting cleanup for the current or later workers. A worker blocked in Redis or Kafka can therefore outlive `SpanFlusher.join`, leaving multiple daemon workers running after the consumer has shut down or rebalanced. Apply the deadline to waiting, but still terminate/join every worker after the deadline is reached.

findings.title: Inserting max_processes breaks positional produce_to_pipe callers
findings.body: `produce_to_pipe` was the third optional positional argument to `SpanFlusher`; adding `max_processes` before it changes `SpanFlusher(buffer, next_step, callback)` to treat the callback as a process count. Construction then fails when `min` compares that callable with the shard count. Preserve the existing positional contract by placing `max_processes` after `produce_to_pipe` or making the new argument keyword-only.

findings.title: Invalid flusher process counts are accepted and crash initialization
findings.body: The new option accepts arbitrary integers. With `--flusher-processes -1` and any assigned shard, `SpanFlusher` computes `num_processes == -1`, creates an empty process map, and then raises `KeyError` when assigning the first shard to index 0. A value of zero also silently means one process per shard because of the `or` fallback, contrary to the stated maximum. Restrict the Click option to positive integers (and validate direct construction similarly).

findings.title: The new process-limit test only runs thread-based workers
findings.body: Passing a non-null `produce_to_pipe` forces `SpanFlusher` to use `threading.Thread`, so this test never executes the spawn-process branch used in production. It only inspects the shard map and does not verify that multiple spawned workers can initialize, flush, restart, or shut down. Add coverage using actual spawn workers and process-safe output/producer mocking; this would exercise the new lifecycle code.
